Second: We say: it is not necessarily the case that what is meant is that they will be seized with the same visible sensory punishment that those received, namely the quaking and the cry that destroyed them all to the last one. What may be meant is the sickness of the heart, which is arrogance, aversion, and rejection of the truth.

﴿When it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time."﴾ This "time" was three days, the end of three days. ﴿But they defied the command of their Lord﴾ (51:44), and did not turn back from their error. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on﴾. The thunderbolt which was their destruction was a quaking and a cry. ﴿While they were looking on﴾: that is, some of them were looking at others, collapsing and falling down dead.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 45:

﴿So they were not able to stand up, nor were they among those who could help themselves.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 45] That is: they were not able to stand up. "Nor were they among those who could help themselves": that is, none of them was able to help another; rather, they were all destroyed to the last one.

Thus does God, exalted is He, deal with those who denied His messengers, may prayers and peace be upon them. However, the total annihilating punishment has been lifted from this Ummah, for the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his Lord, glorified and exalted is He, not to destroy them with a general famine [[Recorded by Muslim (2889/19) from the hadith of Thawban, and (2890/20) from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.]] – that is, a general punishment – but they were afflicted with something else: that some of them would kill others and take others captive. And so it has happened. This Ummah has not been struck with a general punishment as the nations before it were, but it has been struck with God making its violence (ba's) among themselves, since the era of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs; as they disagreed over 'Uthman and over 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and strife occurred, and it continues to follow one another until this day of ours.

Then, this Ummah whose violence God has made among themselves is not only the Ummah of response (ummat al-ijabah) alone, but the Ummah of response and the Ummah of call (ummat al-da'wah). For this reason we say: whatever strife and calamity has occurred on earth, in its east and its west, from disbelievers and non-disbelievers, is only a consequence of sins; and it is the punishment of this Ummah that God makes them taste the violence of one another.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 46:

﴿So they were not able to stand [against it], nor were they victorious﴾ [45] ﴿And the people of Noah before them. Indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient﴾ [46]

Meaning: remember ﴿the people of Noah before them﴾, who were the first nation to which a messenger was sent. But they denied him. This messenger, Noah (peace be upon him), remained among them for nine hundred and fifty years, calling them to Allah, reminding them and admonishing them, yet they, may Allah protect us, did not believe: ﴿None believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud 40]. So much so that he (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Every time I call them that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and draw their garments over themselves﴾ [Nuh 7]. ﴿They put their fingers in their ears﴾ so that they would not hear what he says. ﴿And draw their garments over themselves﴾, i.e., they covered themselves with them so that they would not see him, we ask Allah for well-being. This is the utmost of hatred toward what he says and does. ﴿They draw their garments over themselves, and persist﴾ in their falsehood, ﴿and are arrogantly proud, with great arrogance﴾ [Nuh 7].

The last thing he (peace be upon him) said was: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers, a dweller﴾ [Nuh 26], and he called upon his Lord: ﴿I am overpowered, so give victory﴾ [al-Qamar 10]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down, and caused the earth to burst forth with springs, so the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ [al-Qamar 11, 12].

And for this reason, Allah knows best, they will have a share of the punishment of the deniers, because they were the first nation to deny the messengers. Whoever initiates an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of those who act upon it until the Day of Resurrection, just as whoever kills a soul, upon the son of Adam who killed his brother falls a share of [the sin], and a share of the punishment of the killer until the Day of Resurrection.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength (bi-aydin), and indeed, We are expanding it.﴾ [al-Dhariyat 47] In this verse Allah, exalted is He, informs that He built the heaven ﴿with strength (bi-aydin)﴾, meaning with power, as He said: ﴿And We built above you seven strong (heavens)﴾ [al-Naba' 12]. The word aydin is not the plural of yad (hand), as some people imagine, thinking that the meaning is that Allah built the heaven ﴿with aydin﴾, meaning with His hands, Mighty and Majestic. That is because aydin here is a verbal noun (masdar) of (ada ya'idu), meaning "to be strong." For this reason Allah did not attribute this word to His noble Self, as He attributed it to His Self in His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We created for them, of what Our hands have done, livestock, so that they are their owners?﴾ [Ya-Sin 71]. Whoever interprets aydin here as "strength" is not to be called one of those who distort the words from their places (ta'wil); rather, it is correct interpretation (ta'wil sahih).

﴿And indeed, We are expanding it﴾ meaning: We are expanding its expanses, because it is vast, great, and encompassing the earth from every side.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 48:

﴿And the earth – We spread it out⁠﴾. That is: We made it for its inhabitants like a soft, comfortable bed (firash).

﴿So how excellent are We as the Spreaders⁠﴾. He, blessed and exalted, praised Himself by this, because He is worthy of praise. Allah, blessed and exalted, made the earth – I mean the earth – made it level and beneficial for the servants. It is not so hard that people cannot benefit from it, nor so soft that they cannot settle upon it; rather it is perfectly suited to them. Yet there is variation in its softness and hardness, but this does not prevent benefiting from it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 49:

﴿And of everything We created pairs, that perhaps you may remember.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 51:49] Allah, blessed and exalted is He, created from everything two opposites in pairs, so that the state of things is complete and becomes fit through the joining of one to the other. So all animals, both humans and others, come from two pairs of male and female, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another.﴾ [al-Hujurat 49:13] However, Adam, peace be upon him, was created by Allah with His own hand, without a mother or a father; and his wife Hawwa' (Eve) was created from a father without a mother; and 'Isa (Jesus) son of Maryam was created from a mother without a father. For this reason, people divide humankind into four categories:

The first: one who was created without a mother or a father, and that is Adam.

The second: one who was created from a father without a mother, and that is Hawwa'.

The third: one who was created from a mother without a father, and that is 'Isa.

The rest of humankind were created from a male and a female.

From everything Allah created two pairs: dryness and moisture, heat and cold, softness and hardness, and other things which, when a person reflects upon them, he recognizes thereby the wisdom of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

﴿That perhaps you may remember﴾: that is, We have made that clear to you so that you may remember and take admonition from the signs of Allah, blessed and exalted is He. Indeed, the more a person knows of the signs of Allah, whether cosmic (kawniyyah) or legislative (shar'iyyah), the more he takes admonition and draws lessons. For this reason Allah urged reflection upon the cosmic signs, saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe.﴾ [Yunus 10:101], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they not reflect within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth.﴾ [ar-Rum 30:8], and Allah, exalted is He, praised those who reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth in His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding (190), who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; exalted are You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire."﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:190-191] Therefore, a person should take admonition, remember, and reflect upon the cosmic and legislative signs of Allah, glorified is He.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 50:

﴿So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 50] This is as if it were on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, meaning: say to them, "Flee to Allah. ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him﴾ — that is, from Allah — ﴿a clear warner.﴾"

Fleeing to Allah takes place by standing in obedience to Him and avoiding His prohibitions, for nothing rescues you from the punishment of Allah except this: that you stand in obedience to Allah. So when a person stands in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it is as if he has fled from an enemy. Have you seen that if a violent, roaring valley came rushing towards you, would you stand before it? No, you would not stand before it; rather, you would flee from it and run away from it. Likewise, if a blazing fire came towards you, you would not stand but would flee. Likewise, the Fire of Hell is more severe, greater, and more deserving of fleeing from than these. Therefore He said: ﴿So flee to Allah﴾, that is, from the punishment of Allah. ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner﴾, that is, a warner, ﴿a clear﴾, that is, one who makes manifest what they were warned of and makes it clear to them.

He, peace and blessings be upon him, is a warner from Allah, the Exalted, to His servants: he warns those who oppose His command of punishment. And along with this, he ﷺ is also a bringer of good news: a bringer of good news to those who believe and obey, of Paradise and felicity in this world and the Hereafter, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.﴾ [an-Nahl: 97]. However, Allah, blessed and exalted, mentions warning only in the context of threat and intimidation. And this surah, as you can all see, contains mention of the earlier nations and the punishment that befell them for opposing the command of Allah, blessed and exalted.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 51:

﴿And do not set up with Allah another god. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 51] That is: do not take with Him any deity that you worship. ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾ Worshipped things are of various kinds and categories. Among people there are those who worship the sun, some who worship the moon, some who worship the stars, some who worship animals, some who worship trees, some who worship stones, and some who worship wealth. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Woe to the slave of the dinar, woe to the slave of the dirham, woe to the slave of the khamisah, woe to the slave of the khamilah; if he is given, he is pleased, and if he is not given, he is displeased."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2886) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and it does not contain "woe to the slave of the khamilah."]] The Messenger (ﷺ) thus clarified that the one whose only concern is wealth is, in reality, a worshipper of it, even if he does not bow or prostrate to it. Yet the attachment of his heart to it, his preoccupation with it, and his being pleased when he obtains it and displeased when it is withheld undoubtedly mean that it has completely taken control of his heart. However, the forms of worship differ in their ruling: if he directs some act of worship to it, this is major shirk; but if he directs no act of worship to it, yet his heart is wholly attached to it, to the extent that he abandons obligations and commits prohibitions in order to obtain it, then this is a form of worship that does not take one out of the religion, but is truly worship. ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾ He repeated this because of the importance of the subject.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 52:

﴿Thus did there not come to those before them any messenger but they said, "A magician or a madman!"﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 52]. Meaning: the matter that befell you, O Muhammad, has befallen those before you. His saying, ﴿Thus﴾, is the predicate of an omitted subject; the estimate is: "The matter is thus," meaning: the affair of the earlier nations is like the affair of these who denied you, O Muhammad. He explained this "thus" by His saying: ﴿there did not come to those before them any messenger but they said, "A magician or a madman!"﴾, meaning: no messenger came to them but they said such things. The ﴿min﴾ in His saying ﴿any messenger (min rasul)﴾ is grammatically superfluous (za'idah), like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Lest you should say, "There came to us no bearer of good tidings and no warner"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19]; the meaning is: "There came to us a bearer of good tidings and a warner," but letters are sometimes added in some sentences for emphasis.

So ﴿there did not come to those before them any messenger﴾ means: no messenger came to them but they described him with these two descriptions: ﴿"A magician or a madman!"﴾. "Magician" with regard to his influence, his clarity and his eloquence, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, there is magic in eloquence"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5146) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.]].

﴿"Or a madman!"﴾ meaning: or they said "madman" with regard to his conduct, because this conduct, in the view of these deniers, is madness; we ask Allah for well-being. In this there is consolation for the Messenger ﷺ, because when a person knows that others have suffered what he has suffered, he is consoled by that and the matter becomes easier for him. For this reason al-Khansa', Tumadir, said while lamenting her brother Sakhr in one of her elegies:

Were it not for the abundance of those weeping around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.
And they do not weep like my brother, but I console myself for him by taking example (at-ta'assi).

The saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, also indicates this: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 39]; because when another shares a person's punishment, it becomes easier for him, but on the Day of Resurrection it does not benefit a person that another shares his punishment.

The point is that in this sentence, with regard to the Messenger ﷺ, there is consolation for him so that he does not grieve, for what befell him has befallen others. It also indicates that the ways of those who deny the messengers are one, even if their times are far apart and their regions are distant, because the criminal is the brother of the criminal, so the way is one.

"Has this saying been passed down from one to another? Rather, they are a people who transgress."

That is, by this statement. ﴿Has this saying been passed down from one to another?﴾ ﴿Rather, they are a people who transgress.﴾ This means: are these deniers of the messengers, who agreed in describing the messengers as sorcerers and madmen, did they arrange this among themselves? That is, did each of these nations write a charge to the nations that followed, saying: "Say to your prophets, 'You are sorcerers and madmen'"? The answer is no, and for this reason He said: ﴿Rather, they are a people who transgress.﴾ This is a turning away that nullifies (idrab ibtal), meaning: no such arrangement took place, but rather similar thoughts arose in their minds (tawaridat al-khawatir), because their goal was one, namely denying the messengers, so their words agreed. In His saying ﴿transgress﴾ is a description that these are tyrants who overstep. And this is among the greatest forms of tyranny, we seek refuge in Allah, that they describe the callers to truth as sorcerers and madmen.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So turn away from them﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 51:54], meaning: turn away from these people, and do not concern yourself with them.

﴿for you are not to be blamed﴾ means: no one will blame you, because you have conveyed the message, fulfilled the trust, and endured patiently and persevered. The Prophet (ﷺ) indeed endured patiently and persevered against the harm of the Quraysh and their humiliation of him, but the final outcome was his, all praise be to Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Turn away from them﴾, meaning: you should not exhaust yourself over them, nor destroy yourself over them. In this state you are not blamed for that, because he (ﷺ) had done what was required of him.

Regarding Allah's words ﴿Turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed﴾, there are two matters in it:

The first matter: the excusing of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the establishing of an excuse for him.

The second: a warning to these deniers, that Allah the Exalted threatens them with the Messenger's turning away from them, because there is no good in them.

﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 55]. ﴿Remind﴾, i.e., remind people of the signs of Allah, of His legislation and of His days. His legislation is what Allah has made obligatory upon the servants. His days are His punishment, may He be blessed and exalted, of those who deny, and His reward of those who obey. However, Allah left the reminder unrestricted, saying ﴿remind﴾ and not saying "remind the believers," but He made clear that those who benefit from the reminder are the believers. He said: ﴿for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾, because the believer, when reminded, is as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described him: ﴿When they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, they do not fall down before them deaf and blind﴾ [Al-Furqan: 73]. Rather, they accept them with complete openness of heart and complete tranquility.

* In the verse is evidence for the obligation of reminding in every circumstance.

* In it is also: that those who benefit from the reminder are the believers, and that whoever does not benefit from the reminder is not a believer, either lacking faith altogether or having deficient faith. Here, examine yourself: when you are reminded of the signs of Allah and warned about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, do you remember, or does your heart remain hard as it was? If it is the first, then praise Allah, for you are among the believers. If it is the second, then take account of yourself and blame no one but yourself. You must return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until you benefit from the reminder.

* In the verse is also evidence that the stronger the faith, the greater and more intense the benefit from the reminder. This is from a well-known principle among the scholars (qa'idah, a legal maxim), which is: when a ruling is attached to an attribute, it increases with the increase of that attribute and decreases with its decrease.

Regarding His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾. That is, I did not bring them into existence after non-existence except for this great wisdom, which is the worship of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, alone, with no partner, except for the worship of Allah, Exalted is He alone, as we will explain. The lam in His saying ﴿that they should worship Me﴾ is the lam of causation (ta'lil). However, this causation is a legislative causation (ta'lil shar'i), meaning: for the purpose that they worship Me, by My commanding them so that they comply with My command. The lam here is not a causation of decree (ta'lil qadari), because if it were a causation of decree, then all the jinn and mankind would have to worship Him. Rather, the lam here is to clarify the legislative wisdom in the creation of the jinn and mankind.

As for the jinn, they are an unseen world, created from fire, because their father is Iblis, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you?﴾ [al-Kahf 50].

They were called jinn because they are concealed from the eyes, for they see us and we do not see them. This is the basic principle: they are an unseen world, but they may appear at times. The basic principle regarding them is that, like mankind, some of them are Muslims and some are not, some are righteous and some are below that. However, mankind is superior to them because they are better in terms of origin, as they were created from clay, from dust, from clay like pottery. As for those jinn, they were created from fire. Likewise, mankind is distinguished from them in that among mankind there are messengers and prophets, whereas among the jinn there are no messengers. Yes, among them are warners who convey the messages to mankind, as in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And [mention] when We directed to you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an. So when they attended it, they said, "Be silent." And when it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners﴾ [al-Ahqaf 29]. Observe their courtesy in their saying ﴿Be silent﴾, then their remaining until the gathering ended, then they departed as callers after they had heard: ﴿They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses"﴾ [al-Ahqaf 29–30], to the end of the verse.

As for mankind, they are the children of Adam, the human beings. These were created for one thing: the worship of Allah, not so that they benefit Allah by their obedience, nor so that they harm Him by their disobedience, nor so that they feed Him. Hence He said: ﴿I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want that they should feed Me﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 57], meaning: I do not seek from them sustenance, that is, a gift from which I would benefit, nor that they feed Me so that I benefit from their feeding. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, while He feeds but is not fed?"﴾ [al-An'am 14]. So He, Exalted is He, possesses self-sufficiency, generosity and munificence, and He is free of need of anything other than Himself.

So if we ask: What is the wisdom behind the creation of the jinn and mankind? What is the wisdom? Worship. That is, they were not created so that they would populate the earth, nor so that they would eat, nor so that they would drink, nor so that they would enjoy themselves as cattle do, but they were created to worship Allah, and what is on the earth was created for them. We are created for worship, and what is on the earth is created for us: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 29]. And it is strange that our people now busy themselves with what was created for them, away from what they were created for. What was created for them? What is on the earth. Away from what they were created for, which is worship. This is foolishness, that they occupy themselves with something created for them while neglecting the thing for which they were created.

So what is worship? We say that it is applied to two meanings. The first meaning: ta'abbud (devotional act), that is, the act of the servant; it is said: "He worshipped Allah with worship (ta'abbud)." The second: that which is worshipped (al-muta'abbad bihi), which is 'ibadah. About this meaning, Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is a comprehensive term for everything that Allah loves and is pleased with, of statements and deeds, outward and inward, and everything that brings one closer to Allah. Thus it is a comprehensive term for everything: prayer is worship, charity is worship, fasting is worship, Hajj is worship, enjoining good is worship, forbidding evil is worship; every statement or action that brings one closer to Allah is worship.

Therefore, worship is applied to two meanings: the first meaning: ta'abbud, which is the act of the servant.

And the second meaning: al-muta'abbad bihi, which is worship itself.

Therefore, worship is applied to two meanings: the first meaning: ta'abbud, which is the act of the servant.

And the second meaning: al-muta'abbad bihi, which is worship itself.

﴿مَا أُرِيدُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ وَمَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ يُطْعِمُونِ﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 57, 58]: "I do not want any provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me." ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ﴾: "Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm."

﴿هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ﴾ means: He is the Possessor of giving, who gives. Thus *rizq* (provision) here means *ʿaṭāʾ* (giving). From this is the Almighty's saying: ﴿وَإِذَا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ أُولُو الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينُ فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ﴾ [An-Nisa: 8], "And when the relatives, the orphans and the needy are present at the division, provide for them from it," meaning: give them. The word ﴿الرَّزَّاقُ﴾ is more emphatic than *al-Rāziq* (the Provider), because *al-Razzāq* is an intensive form (*ṣīghat mubālagha*), indicating abundance of provision and abundance of those provided for. The provision of Allah the Exalted is abundant in terms of the multitude of those who receive it: every creature on the earth has its provision guaranteed by Allah, human and animal, flying and crawling, small and large.

Can we count the kinds of creatures that are on the earth? It is not possible. If I said to you, "Count the species that are on the earth," you would not be able to, let alone their individuals. Every individual of them is one whose provision Allah the Exalted has guaranteed: ﴿وَمَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا﴾ [Hud: 6], "There is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah." Since this is the case, Allah's provision is abundant in terms of those who receive it. Who can count those who are provided for? No one can count them. It is also abundant in terms of each one of them. How much provision do you have from Allah? It is abundant and uncountable. Allah's provision to you encompasses you night and day: your intellect, your health, your wealth, your children, your security, and countless other things. ﴿وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا﴾ [An-Nahl: 18], "And if you should count the favours of Allah, you could not enumerate them." For this reason the name *al-Razzāq* came with the doubling of the letter *dāl* (*tashdīd*), which indicates abundance.

His saying ﴿ذُو الْقُوَّةِ﴾ means: the Possessor of a strength that has no strength opposing it, as the pre-Islamic poet said:

Where is the refuge, when the Seeking God is pursuing?
And the broken-nosed one is defeated, and there is no victor.

Although this is from the pre-Islamic period, the strength of Allah the Mighty and Majestic has no equal. His strength, the Mighty and Majestic, is never touched by weakness, unlike the strength of the created being. The strength of the created being ends in weakness, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وَشَيْبَةً يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْقَدِيرُ﴾ [Ar-Rum: 54], "Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful." As for the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, weakness does not reach His strength in any way. When ʿĀd said: ﴿مَنْ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةً﴾ [Fussilat: 15], "Who is stronger than us in strength?", what did Allah say? ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُمْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً﴾, "Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is stronger than them in strength?" And Allah the Mighty and Majestic has spoken truly.

His saying ﴿الْمَتِينُ﴾ means: the Firm, the Severe. He is firm in His strength, firm in His punishment, and firm in everything in which wisdom requires firmness. Consider Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي فَاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ [An-Nur: 2], "The adulterous woman and the adulterer—lash each one of them a hundred lashes, and do not let pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day." This is severity: ﴿لَا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ﴾, "do not let pity take hold of you." Allah the Mighty and Majestic is the Most Merciful of the merciful, and yet He commands us, indeed forbids us, to let pity for the adulterous woman and the adulterer take hold of us: ﴿لَا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ﴾. This is evidence of strength.

Among His strength, the Mighty and Majestic: He, glorified and exalted, created the heavens and the earth in six days. Did He grow weary? No: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 33], "Did they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation?"

Among His strength and power: He, Majestic and Exalted, will resurrect people as a single soul: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ (١٣) فَإِذَا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 13, 14], "It will be but a single shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth." Examples of this are many. He, Majestic and Exalted, possesses the utmost strength, which no other strength can rival.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, for those who have wronged, there is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 59]. Those who wronged by disbelief have a portion (dhanub) like the portion of their companions. The word dhanub (a bucket, or whatever is used to draw water) originally means the bucket, or that with which water is drawn. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Pour over his urine a bucket (dhanub) of water."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (220) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] The meaning is: these wrongdoers have a share like the share of those who came before them. ﴿Indeed, for those who have wronged, there is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾, i.e., a share of punishment like the share of their companions.

Notice how Allah called the earlier peoples of distant times "companions" of these: this is because they agree in denying the messengers and in attributing to them what they do not deserve. They are truly companions, even though the times and places are far apart.

﴿So let them not ask Me to hasten﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 56]. The nun here is kasra-vowelled, being the nun of protection (nun al-wiqayah, the vowel-protecting nun placed before the pronoun), and the pronoun ya' has been dropped; the original is: fa-la yasta'jiluni ("so let them not hasten Me"), and the ya' was dropped for lightness. Therefore a person should not be confused, asking: how is there a nun when "la" is a prohibitive? The answer is that we say: this nun is not the nun of i'rab (grammatical inflection), but the nun of protection, so the verb is jussive (majzum), the nun is for protection, and the ya' which is the object is omitted.

In His saying ﴿So let them not ask Me to hasten﴾ there is a clear threat: that this punishment will surely come to them, but they should not hasten Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer and delays him, until when He seizes him He does not let him go. As came in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not release him," and he recited the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud 102].[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4686) and Muslim (2583/61) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 51, verse 60:

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, from their Day which they are promised.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 60] "Woe" (wayl) means a threat and punishment. The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, threatens them with this Day which they are promised, and it is the Day of Resurrection. For they will find that what was sent to them was true, and they will find humiliation and disgrace, ﴿on a Day when some faces will turn bright and some faces will turn dark﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106], and ﴿We will gather the criminals on that Day with blue eyes﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102]. So this will be from among the matters of that world; we ask Allah for well-being in this respect. Therefore He said: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, from their Day which they are promised﴾. This Day will be a difficult day for them, because they are disbelievers, and we seek refuge in Allah.
